findings.title: parseQuantity does not validate or provide a radix, allowing NaN/invalid quantities into cart math
findings.problem: parseQuantity passes the raw customer-entered text directly to parseInt without a radix argument and without checking the result. Non-numeric or malformed input (e.g. "abc", "", "1e5", "-3") yields NaN or a negative number, which is returned to the caller unchecked.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate input with Number.isInteger after parsing, reject/clamp NaN and negative values, and specify a radix, e.g. `const n = parseInt(text, 10); if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n < 0) throw new Error('INVALID_QUANTITY'); return n;`

findings.title: applyDiscount does not validate that percent is within the documented 0-100 range
findings.problem: The docstring states percent should be 0-100, but applyDiscount performs no bounds checking. A percent value below 0 increases the total; a value above 100 makes the result negative.
findings.recommendedFix: Clamp or validate percent: `if (percent < 0 || percent > 100) throw new Error('INVALID_DISCOUNT_PERCENT');` before computing, or clamp with Math.min/Math.max.

findings.title: applyDiscount, parseQuantity, and all of session.js lack test coverage
findings.problem: The only test file present exercises solely the subtotal() function. applyDiscount() and parseQuantity() in cart.js, and the entire session.js module (createSession, isExpired, refresh), have no automated tests in the provided snapshot.
findings.recommendedFix: Add unit tests for applyDiscount (including boundary/invalid percent values), parseQuantity (including invalid input), and session.js (expiry boundary, refresh behavior on expired sessions).
